provider_policy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

provider_policy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

Which authoritative master-system identifier designates this decision, and which registry mints and resolves it?
What version discriminator distinguishes this expression of the decision from earlier or later expressions of the same decision?
Is the identifier scoped to the decision content itself or to the record that carries it, and how is that distinction represented?
Which prior decision, if any, does this decision supersede, amend, reaffirm or reverse, and by which identifier?
Which external or jurisdictional identifiers are carried as labelled alternate identifiers for this decision?
Which decision type does this record instantiate, and under which controlled classification scheme is that type published?
Which jurisdiction, regulatory regime or institutional profile governs the content this decision must carry?
Does the decision produce legal or similarly significant effects for an identified natural person, and is it based solely on automated processing?
Which content elements must be present for a decision of this type and profile to be treated as complete?
How is this decision type distinguished from a legal judgment or from an executable business rule covering the same subject matter?
What single question does this decision answer, stated so that a recorded answer can be checked against it?
What is the admissible answer space for that question, and is it an enumerated set or an open expression?
What problem, need or issue made this decision necessary, and which upstream item raised it?
Is this an atomic decision, or does it decompose into sub-decisions that must be settled for the answer to hold?
Which objectives is the decision intended to achieve, expressed specifically enough to be measurable?
Which critical success factors must any acceptable option possess for the objectives to be delivered?
Which performance indicators or outcome measures are expected to be affected, and in which direction?
By when are the desired effects expected to be realised, and over what appraisal period are they assessed?
Which subjects, populations, assets or system elements are affected by this decision?
Over what geographic, organisational or system extent does the decision apply?
Which input data, upstream decisions and knowledge sources does this decision depend on?
Which concerns or stakeholder interests does the decision pertain to, and which of them does it leave unaddressed?
Which assumptions about the context are declared, and which of them are known to be unverified?
Which hard constraints must any selected alternative satisfy, and which external requirement does each constraint cite?
Which constraints express a budgetary, temporal or capacity limit, and what value and unit does each carry?
Which stated conditions are soft preferences rather than binding constraints, and how is that distinction recorded?
What happens to an alternative that violates a binding constraint, and can a waiver admit it despite the violation?
Which decision rules map the stated inputs to admissible outcomes for this decision?
When several rules match, which conflict-resolution or hit policy is declared, and does it yield a single result or several?
Which external executable rule, policy or model is cited as the source of the applied rules, and at which version?
How is a discretionary outcome, where no rule determines the answer, distinguished from a rule-determined one?
Which candidate alternatives were placed under consideration, and how is each identified within this decision?
Is a no-action, business-as-usual or do-minimum baseline included, and if not, on what stated basis is it absent?
How are variants of the same alternative distinguished from genuinely distinct alternatives?
What does each alternative commit to doing, described in terms sufficient for it to be evaluated against the declared criteria?
Which screening or mandatory criteria decide whether an alternative is eligible for detailed evaluation?
Which alternatives were eliminated from detailed study, and what reason is recorded against each?
Which recorded screening stage does each exclusion cite, and was the exclusion by filter rating, mandatory-criterion failure or constraint violation?
Can an excluded alternative be reinstated, and what would have to change for that to happen?
Which criteria compare the alternatives, and what measure, scale and unit does each criterion use?
Are the declared criteria mutually independent and non-overlapping, and how was that checked?
What weight does each criterion carry, and by which declared weighting method were the weights derived?
Which criteria are mandatory pass-or-fail and which are trade-off criteria whose shortfall can be compensated?
Are any criteria monetised, and if so under which appraisal convention and price base?
What result does each alternative achieve on each declared criterion, in the criterion's own measure?
What ranking or comparison follows from the recorded results, and by which aggregation was it derived?
How sensitive is the ranking to plausible changes in scores, weights or declared assumptions?
Which evidence items are cited in support of each recorded result, and what role does each citation play?
Which recorded results are contested, provisional or adjusted for known bias?
Which alternative is selected, and is the disposition an approval, refusal, deferral, partial approval or a declared variant of a registered alternative?
What is the explicit outcome statement, phrased as a direct answer to the recorded decision question?
From when does the decision take effect, and for how long or until what event does it apply?
Which factors were expressly balanced in reaching this selection, including any consideration of overriding policy?
How does the selection relate to the ranking produced by the evaluation, and is any divergence explained or a preferable alternative named separately?
Which conditions, mitigations or safeguards are attached to the outcome as part of the decision itself?
Which matters are expressly left unresolved, deferred or reserved for a later decision?
Which consequences does the decision state will follow, including accepted risks and residual trade-offs?
Which review or reopening trigger is declared, and what event would cause the decision to be revisited?
Which new concerns or follow-on decisions does this decision raise?
What distinguishes the rationale statement issued with a decision from the individual reason records that compose it?
How is each reason identified so that it can be cited independently of the decision narrative?
What type does each reason carry, and does it argue for or against the recorded outcome?
What relative weight or priority is asserted for a reason, and on which named scale is it expressed?
Which party asserted the reason, and on what stated basis of authority?
Which non-selected alternative does a rejection reason attach to, without restating that alternative's definition?
On what ground was the alternative not selected: infeasible, dominated, non-compliant, outside appetite or deferred?
What condition, if it had been different, is recorded as having made the rejected alternative selectable?
Does the record qualify the rejection as final for this decision or as deferred for later reconsideration?
How are premises and conclusions distinguished within a recorded argument, and how is the inference between them represented as a first-class element?
Which inference scheme is referenced for each inference step, and where is that scheme catalogue governed?
Which critical questions or exceptions attached to the referenced scheme are recorded, and are they answered?
How are asserted support relations distinguished from asserted conflict relations between argument elements?
Is a given premise recorded as assumed, as axiomatic, or as still requiring support?
Does the record explicitly assert a causal relation, or does it assert only an association observed in the cited material?
For an asserted counterfactual, which antecedent is varied and what outcome is claimed to follow from varying it?
What evidential basis is cited for the causal assertion, and is that basis experimental or observational?
What does the record state about competing explanations or confounding that were considered before the causal claim was made?
Which governed claim does each premise or conclusion slot reference, and by which identifier?
What role does a referenced claim play in this argument: premise, conclusion, context or exception?
How is a locally paraphrased restatement of a claim distinguished from the governed claim it references?
How does this record express which claim version the reasoning relied on, given that claim revision is governed elsewhere?
Which governed evidence item does a citation bind to, and how is an unresolvable reference recorded?
What is the type of the citation act: cited as evidence, cited as authority, cited as quoted, disagreed with or refuted?
How is the specific part of the cited resource pinpointed rather than the resource being cited as a whole?
Does the citation support the reason it is attached to, counter it, or supply context only?
Was the citation asserted by the decision author, or inherited from an intermediate document that cited the source?
What weight did the decision authority give this evidence for this decision, and how is that kept separate from the evidence item's own certainty grade?
Which certainty or quality grade is carried by reference from the evidence model, and which appraisal is asserted locally?
On what stated basis was the cited evidence judged sufficient or insufficient to support the reason it is cited for?
Where cited evidence conflicts, how does the record state which body of evidence was preferred and why?
Which statements are recorded as assumptions rather than as supported premises, and how is that marking made explicit?
On what external condition, input, dataset or third-party commitment does the recorded reasoning depend?
Under what stated condition would an assumption be considered defeated?
For what stated period or context is the assumption asserted to hold?
Who is recorded as responsible for an assumption's continued validity, given that this model performs no monitoring?
What confidence qualifier is attached to the rationale as a whole, and on which named and published scale is it expressed?
Is the qualifier a statement about the evidence, about the inference, or about the outcome holding in practice?
What are the stated limits of knowledge beyond which the recorded reasoning should not be relied on?
How is a calibrated verbal qualifier mapped to a numeric range, and is that mapping published with the record?
Which benefits and disbenefits were traded against each other, and which disbenefits are recorded as knowingly accepted?
Which inputs or assumptions, if changed, are recorded as changing the outcome, and over what stated range were they varied?
What switching value or threshold is recorded at which the preferred option would change?
Are the varied inputs and method disclosed well enough for a qualified third party to see how the result was reached?
Does the record state that no sensitivity analysis was performed, and what reason is given?
What counter-argument or counter-evidence is recorded, and which reason or inference does it attack?
Who raised the objection and in what stated capacity, without this model assigning their role?
How was the objection dispositioned in the rationale: accepted, rebutted, undercut or left open?
Is a minority or dissenting position preserved as an attributed position rather than merged into the majority rationale?
Which argument elements are marked as defeated by a recorded challenge, and what does that marking not change?
What ordered sequence of reasoning steps is recorded as the trace from inputs to the recorded outcome?
For which audience is a rendition produced, and what does the record state was omitted or replaced by a reference for that audience?
How is a rendition asserted to reflect the recorded reasoning rather than a plausible reconstruction of it?
What are the declared bounds of the trace: which steps are recorded in full, which are summarised, and which are not captured at all?
How is each issued rendition identified and linked back to the rationale revision it renders?
Was the rationale authored by a person, generated by a software agent, or generated and then edited by a person?
Which software agent, model version and configuration produced a machine-generated explanation?
At what time was the reasoning asserted, and at what time was the record of it observed or ingested?
From which prior rationale, template or precedent was this reasoning derived?
How is machine-generated explanation labelled so that a reader cannot mistake it for a reason asserted by the decision authority?
Which authoritative master-system identifier designates the body or office that took this decision, and under which mandate instrument did it act?
What subject-matter, monetary or jurisdictional limits does the mandate place on this authority, and what is the recorded consequence of acting outside them?
Over which validity window was the mandate in force at the instant the decision was taken?
Which alternate or successor authority becomes responsible if the deciding body is dissolved, merged or renamed?
Which delegation or sub-delegation steps link the mandate holder to the agent that actually exercised this decision?
What ceiling applies to each delegation step, and is further sub-delegation permitted at that step?
How is a delegation revoked or withdrawn, and what is the effect on decisions already taken under it?
When an act or vote was exercised on behalf of another participant, how is that representation recorded?
Who is the accountable owner of this decision record, and how does that accountability differ from those of the steward, custodian and reviewer?
Which role is answerable for the accuracy of the governance metadata as distinct from the correctness of the decision itself?
How is a role assignment transferred when the holder leaves, and from which instant does the successor's accountability run?
Which role holds the authority to release this decision to a wider audience or to publish it?
Which participants took part, in which declared roles, and which of them were entitled to vote or formally object?
Which decision rule applied — unanimity, qualified or simple majority, consensus, silence or written procedure — and where is that rule prescribed?
Was the participation threshold or quorum asserted as satisfied, by whom, and on what stated basis?
How is a decision taken by written or silence procedure distinguished from one taken in a convened sitting?
How is an abstention or formal objection referenced without reproducing the dissent record owned by the reasoning area?
Which interests were declared by participants in relation to this decision, and against which register entry was each declaration recorded?
Who determined that a declared interest was disqualifying, and what recusal or mitigation action followed?
How does a recusal change the participation threshold or decision rule applied to the affected item?
For how long must interest declarations and conflict determinations remain retrievable after the decision is closed, and under what lawful basis?
Which submission, review, approval and ratification stages did this decision pass, and which of them are mandatory before it can take effect?
Which external approval activity record evidences each stage, and which identifier binds the two?
What distinguishes approval from ratification and from non-binding endorsement in this governance context?
What happens to the decision when a mandatory stage is skipped, completed out of order, or completed by an unauthorised party?
Which status does this decision hold now, and which controlled vocabulary defines the permitted values and the legal transitions between them?
From which instant is the decision effective, and how does that differ from the instants at which it was approved and published?
Which conditions precedent or subsequent must hold for a conditional decision to become or remain effective, and who confirms their satisfaction?
Which follow-up implementation or monitoring obligations are attached by reference, and which model owns their execution?
What causes automatic expiry as opposed to explicit revocation or suspension, and how is each distinguished in the record?
What triggers a scheduled or event-driven review of this decision, and by which due instant must the review occur?
Who may appeal or request reconsideration, to which forum, and within what time limit from which starting instant?
On what grounds may a closed decision be reopened, and which status does it hold while reopened?
How is the outcome of a review, appeal or reconsideration linked to the original decision without overwriting it?
Which version of this decision is authoritative now, and which prior versions does it supersede, consolidate or repeal?
For each ledger entry, which agent made the change, for what stated reason, and under which authority?
How are event time, observation time and ingestion time recorded separately for a single ledger entry?
Which changes are editorial and which are substantive enough to require re-approval or a new version?
Which agents generated, revised and attested the governed decision content, and in which qualified roles did they act?
From which prior decisions, drafts, submissions or precedents was this decision derived?
How are cited claim and evidence records referenced so that their content is not restated in this model?
How is an imported or migrated decision distinguished from one created natively in this Dimension?
What access classification applies, and does it differ between the decision outcome, the rationale and the governance metadata?
Which exemption grounds justify withholding, and can partial access be granted by releasing the parts not covered by them?
When does an embargo lapse so that the decision becomes proactively publishable?
Which register-level metadata remains discoverable even when the content itself is withheld?
Which personal data in participant and interest records must be minimised or masked before disclosure?
Which digest algorithm and value seal each governed version, and which agent computed them at which instant?
Which signature, seal or timestamp-token reference evidences non-repudiation of the approval?
How is a failed integrity verification reported without altering the sealed version?
Which external audit or event-log system holds the trail for this record, and which identifier links the two?
Which retention schedule and issuing authority govern this decision record, and which event starts the retention clock?
Is a legal hold or disposition freeze in force, who imposed it, and when was it released?
When deletion is authorised, which facts survive in the tombstone and which model or Dimension policy executes the disposition?
How is destruction, transfer or migration evidenced so that the disposition remains defensible?
Which decisions are appraised as being of permanent value and transferred to an archival authority rather than destroyed?

requirements: Run a separate no-tools adversarial audit of the active provider result.
Verify the model boundary and entry kind against the frozen relationship contract.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Expose the owner-authorized provider waiver in every publication artifact.
Keep the result reviewable-draft while independent second-provider review is waived.
